## Verdict: PASS — every checklist line passes; F-3 is closed

**F-3 is closed (CONFIRMED).** C-0151 makes C-0149 (2) true in the code rather than narrowing the claim. Each
primitive now reads first and writes after. The reads are the bounded walks, the lookup that a full table refuses, and
the compaction's read of every run. The one write that can still refuse comes first.

* Round r1's probes P1 – P4 were copied unchanged into this seat's scratch mirror. All four are green: each refusal
  leaves the tables exactly as before.
* `malformed.test.ts` gains seven tests. Each compares the whole arena with a structured clone taken before the
  refused call, and each ends on a control that writes, so the comparison is shown to see a write. The case r1 said
  the old hole test could not see is now held: `setFaceHoles` on a face that already holds a run.
* Reverting each write order turns the item's suite red: N01 – N08 and N22 below.
* This seat's own refusal fuzz finds no write before a refusal. It ran 400 random arenas, most with one table entry
  corrupted by hand and some with a full lookup table, and 16 000 random calls. About 8 000 calls were refused; none
  had written first. Reads never wrote either. The control: under N01 – N04 and N06 the same fuzz reports 8 to 73
  writes before a refusal.

The fix round also added one refusal of the same class: the compaction now refuses runs that share entries and do not
fit the pool, where it used to cut them silently. This seat's probe B1 confirms the guard at its exact boundary,
which no test of the item holds (note N-r2-1).

## Notes (no change required for the pass)

* **N-r2-1 — the fit guard's boundary is held by the code but not by a test.** Mutant N11 (`<` → `<=`) leaves the
  suite green. `malformed.test.ts`'s fit test needs 12 entries of 8, so it cannot tell `<` from `<=`. Under N11, shared
  runs that need exactly one entry more than the pool lose their last terminator silently: the write lands past the
  typed array's end. That is the overflow C-0151 (2) says is refused. The code refuses it: probe B1 builds that exact
  case (9 entries of 8) and gets the refusal with the arena byte-identical. It is the same class as round r0's N-5, a
  correct guard that no test holds at its edge. The case is reachable only on a malformed table, and the code is right,
  so it is not a failing line. Suggested at the item's next touch: add B1's case (f's run of three at 0, g starting
  inside it at 1, m's run of one) to the fit test.
* **N-r2-2 — round r0's notes N-3, N-4, N-6 and N-7 stand.** Their files (`walk.ts`, `keys.ts`, the size test) are
  unchanged. N-4 is for M0-a-03 and its checker; N-6 is for the lint's owner.
* **N-r2-3 — scratch receipts in the rows.** C-0149 and C-0151 cite their mutant scripts in the session scratchpad
  (`waves/M0-a-02-fix1/mutants.py`, `waves/build-M0-a-02-fix2/mutants.py`). These are receipts, not the tests that
  hold the rows; the holding tests lie under `plat/`. Other items' rows cite their scratch mutant runs the same way,
  and earlier checkers passed them. The scratchpad does not survive a session (it was moved once already), so the M0
  record (M0-x-01) should cite only the tests and this file, as C-0067 says.

## Verdict: FAIL — one new failing line (F-3), small; F-1 and F-2 are closed

**F-1 is closed (CONFIRMED).** The six unbounded walks of round r0 are bounded and refuse a malformed table with an
`arena:` error. `malformed.test.ts` (new, 10 tests) builds each malformed table — a cyclic set, a set without its
element mark, a set cycling before the row, a set not holding the row, a cyclic key chain, a chain cycling before the
row, a chain ending without it, a cyclic owner list, an owner list without the face, a hole run without its terminator,
a hole run starting outside the pool, a rotation and a ring that never close, full lookup tables under deletion — and
expects each refusal. Every guard's removal turns the item's suite red (§ Mutants: R01 – R07, P01 – P05, W01 – W03, T01 – T05, H01 all red).

**F-2 is closed (CONFIRMED).** `levels.test.ts` now re-stores the face record from each of the six half-edges of its
outer ring and asserts one key, `0,0 100,0`, every time. It also asserts that both visit orders of the doubled vertex
were exercised. Mutant K21 (the tie-break dropped) is red, and so are K21b (the larger successor) and K21c (the last
visit wins).

**The four notes the fix round took up are answered (CONFIRMED).** N-1: C-0149 (4) withdraws C-0146 (3)'s "a role of
the other kind is refused", and the test is retitled and holds the actual reading (an edge role on a vertex slot number
that is also a live half-edge). N-2: the hash values are pinned; this checker recomputed `mix32(1)`, `hash2(0, 0)`,
`hash1(1)` and `hash2(1, 65536)` in Python from the published finaliser and the code's constants and got the pinned
`0x514e28b7`, `0xa8abffde`, `0xb899c278`, `0xfef530e7`. N-5: a test now reads a lattice point whose freed lower slot
still holds it; K27 is red. N-8: C-0149 (5) records the empty signature.

**F-3 (new).** C-0149 (2) records "**A refusal writes nothing.** … so a refused call leaves the tables as they were".
Four refusals that C-0149 (1) itself lists write before they refuse. Probes in a scratch mirror show each one (table in
§ F-3). The hole-run test that names the claim cannot see the main case: it refuses `setFaceHoles` on a face with no
run, so the start that call clears first was −1 already.

## F-3 — C-0149 (2)'s "a refusal writes nothing" is not what the code does

C-0149 (1) names the refusals: the walks, "the three hash probes and both backward-shift deletions by the table's
capacity ('full')". C-0149 (2) then says "A refusal writes nothing … so a refused call leaves the tables as they were",
and its test cell names `malformed.test.ts` ("each refusal, its table untouched").

Reading the code (CONFIRMED by reading), four calls write and then reach a refusal of (1)'s list:

* `removeRoleRow` (`rows.ts:157 – 161`) unlinks the row from its set (and its chain) before `roleHeadDelete`, which
  refuses a full role-head table.
* `addRoleRow` (`rows.ts:98 – 110`) allocates the row and links it into its set before `roleHeadGet` / `roleHeadSet`,
  which refuse a full role-head table.
* `setFaceOwner` (`plat.ts:580 – 602`) unlinks the face from its old owner's list and sets `owner[f]` before
  `ownerGet` / `ownerSet` for the new owner, which refuse a full owner table.
* `setFaceHoles` (`plat.ts:661 – 666`) sets the face's own `holesStart` to −1 before the compaction, which refuses
  another face's run without its terminator. The face loses its holes.

Executed in the scratch mirror `…/scratchpad/waves/check-M0-a-02-r1/mirror/plat`, never in the shared tree
(`probes/zz-r1-probe.test.ts`; `vitest run --project kernel` on that file; log `probe-p1-p4.log`). Each probe corrupts
one table by hand, as `malformed.test.ts` does, and compares the tables before and after the refused call:

| probe | refused call and malformed table | refusal | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `removeRoleRow(r)`, the row alone on its pair; role-head table filled | "a role-head table is full" | `edgeFirst` 0, live 1 | `edgeFirst` **−1**, live 1 (the row live, its set empty, the head still naming it) |
| P2 | `setFaceHoles(f, [two holes])`, f holding a run at 2; g's run without its terminator | "the L0 hole run of face 1 does not end" | starts f 2, g 5, top 7 | f **−1**, g 5, top 7 (f's holes lost) |
| P3 | `addRole(h, way:b)`; role-head table filled | "a role-head table is full" | live 1, set `[0]` | live **2**, set **`[0, 1]`** (a row in the set but in no chain) |
| P4 | `setFaceOwner(f0, block:b)`, f0 in block:a's list; owner table filled | "an owner table is full" | owner[f0] a, a's list `[1, 0]` | owner[f0] **b**, a's list **`[1]`**, b's list absent |

The `malformed.test.ts` hole test (lines 149 – 154) asserts "nothing was written, f's start included", but the call it
refuses is `setFaceHoles(p, 0, k, …)` on a face k with no run. The write at `plat.ts:661` sets k's start from −1 to −1,
so the test cannot fail on it.

The design does not require clean refusals; a refusal is a programming error and nothing repairs the table (C-0149
(2)). But the row records the behaviour as the item's, and the next seats read it: M0-a-06's transactions carry rule 8
("a failed batch leaves the arena at the previous `version`"), and a seat that took C-0149 (2) at its word would not
guard these four paths (PLAUSIBLE, reasoned). This is the class of round r0's F-1 — a recorded behaviour the code does
not have and no test holds (J156: "the tests judge").

**Required change** (lane `build/M0-a-02-fix2`, the item's own files plus a choices row), either:

1. **Make the code hold it.** Look the lookup table up before the first write, so the only write that can refuse comes
   first: `setFaceHoles` clears the face's start only after the compaction (and any growth) has succeeded, or the
   compaction skips that face; `removeRoleRow` does its head-table write (`roleHeadDelete` / `roleHeadSet`) before the
   set and chain writes; `addRoleRow` reads `roleHeadGet` before `allocRow`; `setFaceOwner` reads the new owner's slot
   (`ownerGet`) before the unlink. Add a test per path in `malformed.test.ts` — a target face that already holds a run;
   `removeRoleRow`, `addRole` and `setFaceOwner` against a full lookup table — each asserting the tables unchanged. Or:
2. **Narrow the claim.** A new choices row refining C-0149 (2) names exactly the refusals that write nothing (the
   walks' own refusals inside `removeRoleRow`, the compaction and the backward-shift deletions), and states that a
   lookup-table refusal after an earlier write, and `setFaceHoles`' compaction refusal, leave the tables partly
   written. The hole test's comment "f's start included" is then corrected to what it shows.

Either way the round re-runs P1 – P4 (`probes/zz-r1-probe.test.ts` in this seat's scratch folder; copy it, never into
the shared tree) and the item's whole test set.

## The failing lines

### F-1 — C-0146 (10)'s "every list walk … refuses a malformed table rather than loop" is not what the code does, and no test holds it

The row C-0146 (10) says: "every list walk and probe loop is bounded and refuses a malformed table (a set or chain
that does not end, a full table) rather than loop". Its test cell adds: "the guards on every list walk and probe loop,
which now fail closed".

Reading the code (CONFIRMED by reading):

* **Guarded:** the three hash probes (`tables.ts` `roleHeadSlot` and `ownerSlot`, `handles.ts` `slotOf`), `rowElement`,
  `rowsOn`, `rowsOfKey`, `facesOfOwner`, `nextAt`, `walkRing` and `outgoing`.
* **Unguarded:**
  * `rows.ts:86–92` — `addRoleRow`'s insertion walk, `while (cur >= 0)`.
  * `rows.ts:133–136` — `removeRoleRow`'s set walk. Its `check(t.nextInSet[g] >= 0)` ends a list but not a cycle.
  * `rows.ts:146–149` — `removeRoleRow`'s key-chain walk, the same form.
  * `plat.ts:587–590` — `setFaceOwner`'s unlink walk, the same form.
  * `plat.ts:610` — `faceHoles`' run loop, `for (let i = s; t.holes[i] !== -1; i++)`. Past the pool's end it reads
    `undefined`, which is never −1.
  * `plat.ts:624` — `compactHoles`' run loop, the same form.

Executed in the scratch mirror `…/scratchpad/waves/check-M0-a-02/mirror/plat`, never in the shared tree. Each probe
corrupts one table by hand, runs `vitest run --project kernel <probe>` under `perl -e 'alarm 45; exec @ARGV'`, and
expects the arena to throw:

| probe | malformed table | result |
|---|---|---|
| control | `rowElement` on a set made cyclic (`nextInSet[r1] = r0`) | `Tests 1 passed (1)` — throws "does not end" |
| remove | `removeRoleRow(r2)` on that set | **exit 142** (SIGALRM after 45 s; never returned) |
| owner | `setFaceOwner(f0, −1)`, the owner list cycling `fs3 → fs2 → fs3` | **exit 142** |
| add | `addRole` into a two-row set made cyclic | **exit 142** |
| holes | `faceHoles` with the run's −1 terminator overwritten | **× 17122 ms**, then "Test timed out in 5000ms" — no arena refusal |

`grep -rn "does not end\|not end" packages/kernel/test/arena` finds nothing. No test builds a malformed set, chain,
owner list or hole run, so even the guards that exist can be removed without a red test. Only the full-probe refusals
of the two lookup tables and the handle index are tested (`tables.test.ts` "refuses to probe a full table",
`handles.test.ts` "refuses to probe a full index").

The design does not require fail-closed walks. But the item's own row declares the behaviour and names its proof. The
seat's choice is held by no test and contradicted by the code (J156: "the tests judge").

**Required change.**

1. Bound the six walks as the others are bounded: a step count against the table's `top` or length, and a `check`
   naming the malformed table.
2. Add tests that build each malformed table — a cyclic set, a cyclic key chain, a cyclic owner list, a hole run with
   no terminator — and expect the arena's refusal. Cover the existing guards too (`rowElement`, `rowsOn`, `rowsOfKey`,
   `facesOfOwner`, `nextAt`, `walkRing`, `outgoing`), so that removing any guard turns a test red.

If the round prefers to narrow the claim instead, it needs a new choices row naming exactly the guarded walks. The
guards it keeps still need these tests, because C-0146's test cell says they fail closed.

### F-2 — the face key's "smaller successor" tie-break (§3.3; C-0146 (5)) has a test that cannot fail

`walk.ts:91` keys a face whose ring visits its lowest-leftmost vertex twice on the smaller of the two successors. The
test that names this clause is `levels.test.ts:139` ("a ring that visits its lowest-leftmost vertex twice keys on the
smaller successor"). It reads the key from one stored outer half-edge only. With that start, the first visit is already
followed by the smaller successor.

* **Mutant K21** reduces the condition to `if (c < 0)`, so the first visit wins.
  `vitest run --project kernel test/arena/levels.test.ts` gives `Tests 8 passed (8)`: **SURVIVED**. With
  `resolve.test.ts` added, still `22 passed`.
* **Probe** (in the mirror only): store every half-edge of that ring as the face's `outer` in turn and read
  `faceKey`. Any half-edge of the outer ring is a valid stored outer (`FaceInit.outer`).
  * The original code gives one key: `Tests 1 passed (1)`, key `0,0 100,0`.
  * K21 gives two keys: `AssertionError: expected [ '0,0 100,0', '0,0 50,30' ] to deeply equal [ '0,0 100,0' ]`.

So without the tie-break, the key depends on which half-edge a writer stored. That makes `resolve`'s face order
(`compareFaces`) a function of slot history. §3.3 forbids this: "no implementation ever needs a slot to break a tie";
"No output depends on slot numbers". The item's §3.9 and §6.5 (3) sections say the same ("the one-level view is a
function of levels, never slots"). The code holds the clause, but nothing would catch its loss. Antennae at a corner
are declared faces (§3.10), so the case is real.

**Required change.** Make the test read the key from every half-edge of the ring as the stored outer. Permuted
allocation orders that move the stored start would also do. K21 must then be red.

    the object literal without it, so a required merged field fails `tsc -b` in `arena/plat.ts`, which M0-a-03 does not
    own.
  * §2.2's `LevelIndex.tombstones: Set<number>[]` attached to a `Plat` would break the frozen-copy property. This item's
    `frozen.test.ts` would not notice, because it builds plats without an index. M0-a-03 should keep tombstones in
    typed arrays or outside the `Plat`, or extend the census.
* **N-5 — `vertexAt`'s liveness guard is untested.** Mutant K27 (drop `isVertexLive`) survives. A freed vertex keeps
  its x / y, so it can shadow a live one. A test of `signature` at a point whose earlier vertex was freed and then
  re-created would hold the guard.
* **N-6 — `sortedKeys`.** It enumerates through `Object.assign` into a recording `Proxy`, as C-0146 (7) declares. The
  lint has no exemption for the sanctioned function, so the author used this indirection, which
  `no-object-key-iteration` does not see. It is correct here: the keys are sorted before return (`keys.test.ts`;
  mutant K12 red). The author already flagged it for M0-d-07; the lint's owner may add the exemption and refuse the
  indirection elsewhere.
* **N-7 — `faceWalk` follows writer history.** It returns each ring from its stored half-edge, with holes in stored
  order (C-0146 (2)). A reader whose output depends on ring order or start must canonicalise: M0-d-04's digest, M0-a-15's
  encoder. Nothing changes here.
* **N-8 — equivalent mutants and one unrecorded reading.**
  * Four mutants survive as equivalent:
    * K15 — `compactHoles`' free-face test (`freeFace` always clears `holesStart`).
    * K33 — re-insertion in reverse slot order. Only the layout changes, and "nothing iterates a table" (§2.2).
    * K34 — the hole run's explicit terminator, the author's M22.
    * K35 — a no-op control.
  * `signature` of a lattice point with no vertex returns `{ v: [], e: [] }`. This reading is consistent with §3.11's
    "resolves empty" and with rule 5's "empty signature", and `resolve.test.ts` holds it, but C-0146 does not state it.
    The fix round's row may record it.
